stimuli.title: Error checks on a cash-recycler link
stimuli.content:
A branch's cash-recycling machine talks to its controller over a serial link that uses two error checks.

**Check 1 - code words.** Each command is sent as one of only four valid 6-bit code words:

| Command | Code word |
|---|---|
| IDLE | 000000 |
| COUNT | 001111 |
| DISPENSE | 110011 |
| LOCK | 111100 |

The Hamming distance between two words is the number of bit positions in which they differ. A received word that is not valid is corrected to the nearest valid code word.

**Check 2 - CRC.** Status messages are 4 bits long. The sender appends 3 zeros to the message, divides the result by the generator 1011 using modulo-2 (XOR) division with no carries or borrows, and appends the 3-bit remainder to the message as the CRC.
stimuli.solution: Every pair of valid code words differs in exactly 4 positions, so the minimum distance is 4: up to 3 bit errors are always detected and 1 bit error can always be corrected. 011111 is 1 bit from COUNT (001111). For the message 1101, 1101000 divided by 1011 leaves the remainder 001, so 1101001 is sent.

stimuli.title: CCTV recording system of a branch
stimuli.content:
A branch installs a CCTV system. All figures use decimal units (1 GB = 1,000 MB, 1 TB = 1,000 GB, 1 byte = 8 bits).

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Cameras | 8 IP cameras, each streaming continuously at a constant 4 Mbps (megabits per second) |
| Recorder | Network video recorder (NVR) that records all streams 24 hours a day |
| NVR storage | 6 hard disks of 4 TB each, configured as RAID 6 (two disks' worth of capacity used for parity) |
| Head-office link | 50 Mbps link used to view the cameras live from the regional office |
| Policy | When the disks are full, the oldest recording is overwritten |
stimuli.solution: Total stream = 8 x 4 = 32 Mbps. Per day: 32 Mbps x 86,400 s = 2,764,800 Mb = 345,600 MB = 345.6 GB. RAID 6 usable capacity = (6 - 2) x 4 = 16 TB, and the array survives any two simultaneous disk failures. Retention = 16,000 / 345.6 = 46.3, so 46 full days are kept.

stimuli.title: Firewall rules of a branch
stimuli.content:
A branch firewall checks each new connection against these rules from top to bottom and applies the FIRST rule that matches (protocol, source, destination and destination port must all match). A connection that matches no rule is dropped. The firewall is stateful.

| Rule | Action | Protocol | Source | Destination | Destination port |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Allow | TCP | 10.20.30.0/24 | any | 443 |
| 2 | Deny | TCP | any | any | 3389 |
| 3 | Allow | TCP | 10.20.30.10 | 10.20.0.0/16 | 3389 |
| 4 | Allow | TCP | 10.20.30.0/24 | 10.20.0.25 | 993 |
| 5 | Allow | UDP | 10.20.30.0/24 | 10.20.0.53 | 53 |

The branch LAN is 10.20.30.0/24; head-office servers are in 10.20.0.0/16.
stimuli.solution: Rules are matched in order, so rule 2 blocks all RDP (port 3389) before rule 3 is ever reached; rule 3 must be moved above rule 2. Traffic matching no rule meets the implicit deny. A stateful firewall remembers allowed connections and lets their reply packets back in automatically. Port 993 is IMAP over TLS.

stimuli.title: Complaints received at a bank's cyber cell
stimuli.content:
The cyber cell of a bank logged these four complaints in one week:

1. **Customer Mr. P** got a call from someone claiming to be from the bank's 'KYC team', who asked him to install a 'support app' from the app store and read out a code shown in it. Moments later, the caller could see Mr. P's phone screen, watched him open his banking app, and money was transferred out.
2. **The bank's accounts team** received an email that looked like it came from a regular stationery supplier, from the domain supp1ier-mart.example instead of supplier-mart.example. It said the supplier's bank account had changed and asked that the pending invoice be paid to the new account. The team paid Rs 4.8 lakh.
3. **A branch manager** received a phone call in a voice that sounded exactly like the regional head's, urgently asking her to release a large payment before an audit. The regional head later confirmed he never called; the voice had been generated by software trained on his speeches posted online.
4. **Several customers** of an online store found their card details misused. The store's site was genuine and used HTTPS, but investigators found that attackers had inserted a small JavaScript file into the checkout page that copied card details as they were typed and sent them to the attackers' server.
stimuli.solution: 1: remote-access (screen-sharing) app fraud. 2: business email compromise using a look-alike domain. 3: deepfake voice cloning (AI-generated vishing). 4: formjacking / digital (web) skimming of a checkout page.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the cash-recycler link. The controller receives the invalid word 011111. To which valid code word will it be corrected?

solution.explanation: Count the positions in which 011111 differs from each valid word: from 000000 it differs in 5 positions, from 001111 in 1 (the second bit), from 110011 in 3 and from 111100 in 3. The nearest valid word is 001111 (COUNT), so a single flipped bit is assumed.
solution.shortcut: XOR the two words and count the 1s.
solution.why_others_wrong: IDLE is 5 bits away. DISPENSE and LOCK are each 3 bits away, so they are less likely than a single-bit error from COUNT.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the cash-recycler link. Considering the minimum Hamming distance between the four valid code words, how many bit errors in one word can the code always detect, and how many can it always correct?

options.text: Detect up to 4 bit errors; correct 2 bit errors
Detect up to 3 bit errors; correct 1 bit error
Detect up to 3 bit errors; correct 2 bit errors
Detect up to 2 bit errors; correct 1 bit error

solution.explanation: All six pairs of valid words differ in exactly 4 bits, so the minimum distance d = 4. A code with minimum distance d always detects up to d - 1 = 3 errors (3 flips cannot turn one valid word into another) and always corrects up to floor((d - 1) / 2) = 1 error.
solution.why_others_wrong: Detecting 4 errors is not guaranteed: 4 flips can turn one valid word into another. Correcting 2 errors needs d >= 5. Saying only 2 errors are detected understates the capability.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Detect up to 3 bit errors; correct 1 bit error

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the cash-recycler link. Which 3-bit CRC is appended to the status message 1101?

solution.explanation: Append three zeros: 1101000. Divide by 1011 with XOR: 1101 XOR 1011 = 0110; bring down 0 -> 1100; 1100 XOR 1011 = 0111; bring down 0 -> 1110; 1110 XOR 1011 = 0101; bring down 0 -> 1010; 1010 XOR 1011 = 0001. The remainder is 001, so the frame sent is 1101001.
solution.why_others_wrong: 110 is the remainder if the three zeros are not appended (1101 XOR 1011). 101 is the remainder of ordinary integer division (104 mod 11 = 5), which uses borrows. 111 stops the division after the second step.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A memory dump shows each byte as two hexadecimal digits, for example 3F. How many binary bits does ONE hexadecimal digit stand for?

solution.explanation: 16 = 2^4, so each hexadecimal digit (0 to F) corresponds to exactly 4 bits. Two hex digits make 8 bits, which is one byte.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8 bits is one byte, which needs two hex digits. 16 is the base of the system, not its bit count. 2 bits can show only 4 values.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An ATM's 8-bit status register holds 1011 0110. Bit 2 (counting the rightmost bit as bit 0) is the 'door open' flag. Which single operation switches OFF bit 2 only and leaves all the other bits unchanged?

solution.concept: Bit masking with AND, OR and XOR
solution.explanation: ANDing with 1 keeps a bit and ANDing with 0 clears it. The mask 11111011 has a 0 only in bit 2, so 1011 0110 AND 1111 1011 = 1011 0010: bit 2 is cleared and every other bit is kept.
steps: Need: clear bit 2, keep the rest
solution.why_others_wrong: OR with 00000100 sets bit 2 (it stays 1). XOR with 11111011 flips every bit except bit 2 (gives 01001101). AND with 00000100 clears every bit except bit 2.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A register holds the 8-bit two's-complement value 11101000 (that is, -24). The processor performs an ARITHMETIC right shift by 2 places, which copies the sign bit into the vacated positions. What does the register hold now?

solution.explanation: An arithmetic right shift moves the bits right and refills the left with copies of the sign bit (1 here), so the sign is kept and the value is divided by 2 for each place: -24 / 4 = -6, which is 11111010.
solution.shortcut: Arithmetic right shift by n = divide by 2^n (rounding towards minus infinity).
solution.why_others_wrong: 00111010 is a logical shift that fills with zeros (it reads as +58). 11110100 is a shift by only one place. 10111010 keeps the sign bit but fills the next places with zeros.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The speed of supercomputers used for weather forecasting is compared in units such as petaFLOPS. What does FLOPS measure?

options.text: Frames of light processed per second

solution.explanation: FLOPS (floating-point operations per second) counts how many calculations on real (decimal) numbers a computer completes each second. Supercomputers are ranked in petaFLOPS (10^15) and exaFLOPS (10^18).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up; FLOPS is a rate of floating-point arithmetic.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Floating-point operations per second

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In the usual classification of computer generations, which generation is associated with artificial intelligence, natural-language processing and parallel processing, based on ULSI technology?

solution.explanation: The fifth generation (from the 1980s onwards in most textbooks) aims at intelligent systems: artificial intelligence, natural-language understanding, parallel processing and ULSI chips.
steps: AI + ULSI + parallel processing = fifth generation
solution.why_others_wrong: The first used vacuum tubes, the second transistors and the third integrated circuits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which ancient calculating tool, still used to teach arithmetic, works by sliding beads along rods in a frame?

solution.explanation: The abacus is one of the earliest calculating aids: beads on rods stand for units, tens, hundreds and so on, and numbers are added or subtracted by moving the beads.
solution.why_others_wrong: A slide rule uses sliding logarithmic scales. Napier's bones are numbered rods for multiplication, with no beads. The Pascaline is Pascal's geared mechanical adder.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Second-generation computers replaced vacuum tubes with transistors. Where, and by whom, was the first working (point-contact) transistor demonstrated in December 1947?

options.text: At IBM, by Howard Aiken and Grace Hopper
At Intel, by Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce
At Bell Labs, by John Bardeen and Walter Brattain
At the University of Pennsylvania, by Eckert and Mauchly

solution.explanation: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain achieved transistor action in a germanium point-contact device at Bell Laboratories in December 1947 (working with William Shockley's group). The transistor became the switching element of second-generation computers.
steps: Transistor, 1947 = Bardeen and Brattain at Bell Labs
solution.why_others_wrong: Aiken and Hopper are linked to the Harvard Mark I. Intel was founded in 1968. Eckert and Mauchly built ENIAC, which used vacuum tubes.
solution.final_answer: Option C: At Bell Labs, by John Bardeen and Walter Brattain

fact_checks.claim: CHM Silicon Engine: Bardeen and Brattain achieved transistor action in a germanium point-contact device at Bell Labs in December 1947.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch's server room has four servers but only one keyboard, one monitor and one mouse. Which device lets the administrator control all four servers from that single set by switching between them?

solution.explanation: A KVM (Keyboard, Video, Mouse) switch connects one keyboard, monitor and mouse to several computers and lets the user choose which computer they control at any moment.
steps: One keyboard/monitor/mouse for many computers = KVM switch
solution.why_others_wrong: A network switch connects computers to a LAN. A modem converts signals for a telephone or cable line. A UPS supplies backup power.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: When a program calls a function, the CPU pushes the return address onto the stack in memory and later pops it back. Which CPU register always holds the address of the current top of the stack?

solution.explanation: The Stack Pointer holds the address of the top of the stack. A push stores data there and moves SP; a pop reads from SP and moves it back. Calls, returns and interrupts all use it.
steps: Top of stack address = Stack Pointer
solution.why_others_wrong: The PC holds the address of the next instruction. The IR holds the instruction being executed. The MDR holds data moving to or from memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The microcontroller inside a POS terminal has one memory for program instructions and a separate memory for data, each with its own bus, so it can fetch an instruction and read data in the same cycle. Which architecture is this?

solution.explanation: In the Harvard architecture, instructions and data are kept in separate memories with separate paths, so both can be accessed at once. It is common in microcontrollers and signal processors.
steps: Separate instruction and data memories and buses = Harvard
solution.why_others_wrong: Von Neumann uses one shared memory and path for both. Client-server describes network computing. Pipelining overlaps instruction stages and does not by itself mean separate memories.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A processor runs at 2.4 GHz and, for a bank's batch program, needs on average 1.6 clock cycles per instruction (CPI). What is its rating in MIPS (million instructions per second) for this program?

solution.why_others_wrong: 3,840 multiplies by the CPI instead of dividing. 2,400 ignores the CPI. 667 divides the CPI by the clock in GHz.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An 8-bit processor adds F0 (hex) and 10 (hex). The result is kept in an 8-bit register, and the ALU sets the Carry flag if a carry goes out of bit 7 and the Zero flag if the 8-bit result is zero. What is the outcome?

solution.explanation: F0 + 10 = 100 (hex), which needs 9 bits. The register keeps the low 8 bits, 00, and the 9th bit goes out as a carry, so Carry = 1. The stored result is zero, so Zero = 1.
solution.why_others_wrong: 100 cannot fit in 8 bits. The carry out of bit 7 must be recorded. The Zero flag looks at the stored 8-bit result, which is 00.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Result 00 (hex); Carry flag = 1; Zero flag = 1

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch PC with a little-endian processor sends the IPv4 address 10.20.30.40 (hex 0A 14 1E 28) inside a packet header. Before sending, the program converts the value to network byte order. Which byte goes out first?

solution.explanation: Internet protocols send multi-byte numbers most significant byte first (big-endian), whatever the host's own byte order. Functions such as htonl() convert from host order. The most significant byte of 0A141E28 is 0A, so it is sent first.
steps: Network byte order = most significant byte first
solution.why_others_wrong: 28 is the least significant byte, which a little-endian host stores first in its own memory but which is not sent first. 14 and 1E are middle bytes.

fact_checks.claim: man7 byteorder(3): network byte order, as used on the Internet, is Most Significant Byte first; htonl() converts from host byte order to network byte order.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Before writing code for an EMI calculator, a trainee lists the exact steps: read the loan amount, read the rate, read the tenure, apply the formula, show the EMI. A finite, ordered set of clear steps that solves a problem is called a(n):

solution.explanation: An algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined steps that solves a problem. It can be written in plain language, pseudocode or a flowchart before being coded in any language.
steps: Ordered, finite steps to solve a problem = algorithm
solution.why_others_wrong: A compiler translates programs. An operating system manages the computer. A database stores data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank hires a software firm to build a loan-tracking program designed only for its own procedures and forms, instead of buying a ready-made product sold to many customers. Such software is called:

solution.explanation: Custom (bespoke) software is developed for the specific needs of one organisation. Packaged (off-the-shelf) software is made once and sold to many users.
steps: Built for one organisation's needs = custom software
solution.why_others_wrong: Packaged software is the ready-made alternative the bank chose not to buy. Firmware is stored in a device's chip. Utility software maintains the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An employee copies a licensed office suite from the branch PC and installs it on ten home computers of his friends without buying licences. What is this called?

solution.explanation: Copying, installing or distributing licensed software beyond what the licence allows, without paying for it, is software piracy and infringes the publisher's copyright.
steps: Unlicensed copying of paid software = piracy
solution.why_others_wrong: Open-source and freeware licences allow sharing, but this suite is licensed per installation. Patching means installing fixes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank pays once for a version of an accounting package and may keep using that version for as long as it likes, with no recurring fee (updates to later versions may cost extra). What type of licence is this?

solution.explanation: A perpetual licence is a one-time purchase that gives the right to use the licensed version indefinitely. A subscription licence must be renewed (monthly or yearly) or the software stops being licensed.
steps: Pay once + use indefinitely = perpetual licence
solution.why_others_wrong: A subscription needs recurring payments. A trial ends after a fixed period. Public-domain software has no copyright and needs no purchase.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An analyst writes SELECT branch, SUM(amount) FROM Loans GROUP BY branch; stating WHAT result is wanted rather than the step-by-step procedure to get it. In the generations of programming languages, SQL is usually classed as a:

solution.explanation: Fourth-generation languages are closer to human language and are largely declarative: the user states the result required (as in SQL queries and report generators) and the system works out how to produce it.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1GL is binary machine code and 2GL is assembly with mnemonics. 3GLs such as C and Java are procedural: the programmer writes the steps.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Before a new loan-origination system goes live, branch officers who will actually use it run real business scenarios on it and formally confirm that it meets their requirements. Which testing phase is this?

solution.explanation: User acceptance testing is the final phase, in which the business users verify that the system does what they need in real-world scenarios before it is accepted for production.
steps: End users approve before go-live = UAT
solution.why_others_wrong: Unit testing checks individual modules, usually by developers. Integration testing checks that modules work together. Regression testing re-checks old features after a change.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In an object-oriented banking program, Account is defined once with fields such as balance and methods such as deposit(). Then acc1 and acc2 are created from it, each with its own balance. What are Account and acc1?

options.text: Account is a class; acc1 is an object (instance) of that class
Account is an object; acc1 is a class
Account is a variable; acc1 is a data type

solution.explanation: A class is a blueprint that defines fields and methods. Objects are instances created from the class; each object has its own copy of the fields (acc1 and acc2 hold separate balances).
solution.why_others_wrong: The relationship is the other way round: objects are made from classes. Methods are the functions such as deposit(). Account is not a simple variable.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Account is a class; acc1 is an object (instance) of that class

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A calculator program evaluates expressions in postfix (Reverse Polish) notation using a stack: a number is pushed; an operator pops the top two numbers, applies the operator (second-popped OPERATOR first-popped) and pushes the result. What is the value of  6 2 3 + * 4 -  ?

solution.explanation: Push 6, 2, 3. '+' pops 3 and 2 and pushes 5. '*' pops 5 and 6 and pushes 30. Push 4. '-' pops 4 and 30 and pushes 30 - 4 = 26. The expression is 6 x (2 + 3) - 4 in ordinary notation.
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 forgets the final subtraction. -26 takes the operands of '-' in the wrong order (4 - 30). 8 reads the expression as the infix 6 + 2 x 3 - 4.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Bubble sort arranges a list in ascending order by comparing each pair of neighbours from left to right and swapping them if the left one is larger. After ONE complete pass over the list 42, 17, 58, 9, 33, what is the list?

solution.explanation: Compare 42 and 17: swap -> 17, 42, 58, 9, 33. 42 and 58: no swap. 58 and 9: swap -> 17, 42, 9, 58, 33. 58 and 33: swap -> 17, 42, 9, 33, 58. After one pass the largest value, 58, has 'bubbled' to the end.
solution.why_others_wrong: 9, 17, 33, 42, 58 is the fully sorted list, which needs more passes. 17, 42, 58, 9, 33 stops after the first swap. 17, 9, 33, 42, 58 is the list after the second pass.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A clerk wants to close the active window of the program she has finished using, from the keyboard. Which Windows shortcut does this?

solution.explanation: Alt + F4 closes the active window; if no window is open, it opens the shut-down dialog.
solution.why_others_wrong: Alt + Tab switches between windows. The other two combinations are not the standard close shortcut.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: Alt+F4 - close the active window; if no windows are open, prompt to shut down.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: On a Linux server, an officer wants to display the contents of the text file branch_list.txt on the screen. Which command should he use?

solution.explanation: cat (concatenate) prints the contents of one or more files to the standard output, i.e. the screen.
solution.why_others_wrong: cd changes directory, mkdir creates a directory and pwd prints the current directory; none shows a file's contents.

fact_checks.claim: man7 cat(1): cat - concatenate files and print on the standard output.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An application program wants to read a file from the disk, but ordinary programs run in user mode and cannot control the disk directly. How does the program get the file read?

options.text: It writes directly to the disk controller's registers
It makes a system call, which switches the CPU to kernel mode so that the operating system performs the read
It asks the BIOS to load the file each time
It copies the file into the cache by itself

solution.concept: System calls, user mode and kernel mode
solution.explanation: Hardware access is reserved for the kernel. A program requests services such as file reading through a system call; the CPU switches to kernel mode, the OS checks permissions, performs the I/O and returns the result to the program in user mode.
solution.why_others_wrong: User-mode programs are not allowed to touch device registers directly. BIOS/UEFI services are not used for routine file access by a running OS. Cache is managed by hardware and the OS, not by the program.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It makes a system call, which switches the CPU to kernel mode so that the operating system performs the read

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An operating system allocates memory in fixed pages of 4 KB (4,096 bytes), and a process needs 18,000 bytes. It is given the smallest whole number of pages that can hold it. How much allocated memory is wasted as internal fragmentation?

solution.explanation: 18,000 / 4,096 = 4.39, so 5 pages are needed: 5 x 4,096 = 20,480 bytes. Unused space in the last page = 20,480 - 18,000 = 2,480 bytes.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1,616 is the part of the process in the fifth page, not the unused part. 2,000 wrongly takes 4 KB as 4,000 bytes. 4,096 is a whole page.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's training centre uses flight-style and driving simulators in which trainees control movement by tilting a lever mounted on a base in any direction. Which input device is this?

solution.explanation: A joystick is a lever that pivots on a base; its direction and angle are sent to the computer. It is used in games, simulators and to control machines.
steps: Tilting lever on a base = joystick
solution.why_others_wrong: A light pen points at a screen. A scanner captures images of documents. A plotter is an output device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Printers are classified as impact or non-impact. Which of these is an IMPACT printer?

solution.explanation: Impact printers form characters by physically striking an inked ribbon against the paper. A daisy-wheel printer strikes a wheel of raised characters; dot-matrix and line printers are other impact printers.
solution.why_others_wrong: Laser printers fuse toner, inkjets spray ink, and thermal printers heat special paper; none strikes the paper, so all are non-impact.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A training PC plays recorded lectures through speakers. The audio is stored as digital numbers, but speakers need a continuously varying electrical signal. Which component on the sound card (or audio chip) performs this conversion?

solution.explanation: A DAC turns the stream of digital samples into a continuous analog voltage that drives the speakers or headphones. An ADC does the opposite for microphone input.
solution.why_others_wrong: An ADC converts analog to digital (used for recording). The NIC handles networking and the GPU handles graphics.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A temperature sensor in a data-centre rack outputs 0 to 3.3 V, which a 12-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) turns into numbers. Taking the step size as the full range divided by the number of levels (2^12), what is the smallest voltage change the ADC can distinguish, approximately?

solution.why_others_wrong: 1.611 mV uses 2^11 levels. 12.891 mV is the step of an 8-bit ADC (256 levels). 275 mV divides the range by 12 (the bit count) instead of 2^12.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A display is labelled 1080p while an older broadcast format is 1080i. What does the 'i' mean, compared with 'p'?

options.text: Integrated: the screen has built-in speakers
Inverted: colours are shown in negative
Infrared: the screen uses infrared touch sensing
Interlaced: each refresh draws only alternate lines (odd, then even), while progressive draws every line each time

solution.explanation: In interlaced video each field contains only half the lines (odd lines, then even lines) and two fields make a frame. Progressive scan draws all the lines in every frame, giving smoother motion and sharper text.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other expansions are made up; 'i' and 'p' describe how lines are scanned.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Interlaced: each refresh draws only alternate lines (odd, then even), while progressive draws every line each time

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the CCTV system. If all eight cameras are viewed live from the regional office at the same time, what percentage of the 50 Mbps head-office link do the streams use?

solution.explanation: Total = 8 cameras x 4 Mbps = 32 Mbps. 32 / 50 = 0.64 = 64% of the link.
solution.why_others_wrong: 32% treats the link as 100 Mbps. 16% uses a link of 200 Mbps or 4 cameras at 2 Mbps. 80% is 40 Mbps, as if there were 10 cameras.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the CCTV system. How much storage do the eight cameras use in one full day of recording?

solution.explanation: 32 Mbps x 86,400 seconds = 2,764,800 megabits. Divide by 8 for megabytes: 345,600 MB, and by 1,000 for gigabytes: 345.6 GB.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2,764.8 forgets to convert bits to bytes. 43.2 divides by 8 twice. 14.4 GB is one hour's recording.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the CCTV system. Ignoring formatting overhead, how much usable recording space does the RAID 6 array provide?

solution.explanation: RAID 6 stores two independent parity blocks in every stripe, so two disks' worth of capacity is used for parity: usable = (6 - 2) x 4 TB = 16 TB.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20 TB would be RAID 5 (one parity disk). 24 TB is the raw total with no protection. 12 TB is half the raw capacity, as in mirroring.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the CCTV system. What is the largest number of disks that can fail at the same time without any recording being lost?

solution.explanation: With dual parity, RAID 6 can rebuild the data after any two disks fail together. A third failure before the rebuild finishes would lose data.
solution.why_others_wrong: RAID 5 tolerates only 1 failure and RAID 0 tolerates none. 3 failures exceed the two parity blocks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the CCTV system. When the NVR is full it overwrites the oldest recording. About how many full days of recording does the system keep?

solution.explanation: Usable space = 16 TB = 16,000 GB. Daily use = 345.6 GB. 16,000 / 345.6 = 46.3, so 46 complete days of recording are retained.
solution.why_others_wrong: 57 days uses RAID 5 capacity (20 TB) and 69 days the raw 24 TB. 370 days forgets to convert bits to bytes correctly (43.2 GB a day).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: What is the smallest unit of data that a computer can store, having only the value 0 or 1?

solution.explanation: A bit (binary digit) holds a single 0 or 1. A nibble is 4 bits, a byte is 8 bits, and a word is the processor's natural unit (for example 32 or 64 bits).
solution.why_others_wrong: Nibble (4 bits), byte (8 bits) and word (several bytes) are all made of bits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A branch's body-worn camera and digital camera save photos on a small removable flash card about the size of a postage stamp. What is this storage device usually called?

solution.explanation: SD (Secure Digital) cards, including microSD, are small removable flash-memory cards used in cameras, phones and recorders.
steps: Small removable flash card = SD card
solution.why_others_wrong: A floppy disk is an old magnetic disk in a plastic case. Magnetic tape is used for bulk backups. Blu-ray is an optical disc read by a laser.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Where does cache memory sit in a computer, and why is it used?

options.text: Between RAM and the hard disk, to make the disk larger
Between the CPU and main memory (RAM), to hold frequently used data so the CPU waits less
Inside the monitor, to store screen images
On the network card, to store web pages

solution.explanation: Cache is a small, very fast memory (SRAM) placed between the CPU and main memory. It keeps copies of recently and frequently used data and instructions so that most requests do not have to wait for the slower RAM.
steps: Purpose: reduce the CPU's waiting time
solution.why_others_wrong: Cache does not add capacity to the disk. Screen images are held in video memory. A browser keeps its cache on disk, which is a different meaning of the word.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Between the CPU and main memory (RAM), to hold frequently used data so the CPU waits less

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An SSD controller cannot overwrite a used flash page in place. Before new data can be written there, what must happen?

options.text: The disk must spin up to full speed
The page must be magnetised in the opposite direction
The data must first be copied to the CPU cache
The whole erase block containing that page must be erased first, because flash is written in pages but erased only in larger blocks

solution.concept: NAND flash write and erase granularity
solution.explanation: NAND flash is programmed (written) a page at a time but erased only in much larger blocks of many pages. A used page must be erased before it can be programmed again, so controllers move valid data and erase whole blocks in the background (garbage collection).
solution.why_others_wrong: Flash has no spinning disk or magnetic recording. The CPU cache plays no part in the SSD's internal writes.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The whole erase block containing that page must be erased first, because flash is written in pages but erased only in larger blocks

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: The program in a cheap calculator chip is built into the chip's circuit pattern at the factory and can never be changed by the user or erased. Which kind of ROM is this?

solution.explanation: In mask ROM the data is fixed by the photomask used during manufacturing. It is cheapest in very large quantities but cannot be changed afterwards.
steps: Programmed during manufacture, unchangeable = mask ROM
solution.why_others_wrong: PROM is programmed once by the user after manufacture. EPROM is erased with UV light. EEPROM is erased electrically.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A technician is buying extra RAM for a branch LAPTOP. Laptops use a shorter memory module than the DIMMs of desktop PCs. What is this smaller module called?

solution.explanation: SO-DIMMs are roughly half the length of desktop DIMMs and are used in laptops, mini PCs and some printers and routers.
solution.why_others_wrong: SIMMs are an obsolete older module type. An M.2 SSD is storage, not RAM. CMOS stores firmware settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A DRAM chip has 8,192 rows, and every row must be refreshed once every 64 ms. If the memory controller spreads the refreshes evenly, refreshing one row at a time, how often must it issue a refresh?

solution.explanation: 64 ms must cover 8,192 row refreshes: 64 ms / 8,192 = 0.0078125 ms = 7.8125 microseconds between refresh commands.
solution.why_others_wrong: 128 divides 8,192 by 64 (rows per millisecond, not a time). 0.128 is the reciprocal mistake. 64 microseconds misreads milliseconds as microseconds.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Over a month, a server's operating system writes 100 GB of data to its SSD, but the SSD's controller reports that 250 GB were actually written to the NAND flash (because of garbage collection and moving valid data). What is the write amplification factor?

solution.explanation: Write amplification factor = data written to flash / data written by the host = 250 / 100 = 2.5. Higher values wear the flash out faster; TRIM and over-provisioning help reduce it.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.4 inverts the ratio. 1.5 is the extra 150 GB divided by 100. 3.5 adds the two figures.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the firewall rules. A clerk's PC, 10.20.30.44, sends a DNS query over UDP to 10.20.0.53 on port 53. What happens?

options.text: Rule 1 matches and the query is allowed
Rule 2 matches and the query is denied
No rule matches, so the query is dropped
Rule 5 matches and the query is allowed

solution.explanation: Rules 1 to 4 are for TCP, so a UDP packet cannot match them. Rule 5 is UDP from 10.20.30.0/24 to 10.20.0.53 port 53: the source 10.20.30.44 is inside the /24, so rule 5 matches and allows it.
steps: Protocol UDP -> rules 1-4 do not apply
solution.why_others_wrong: Rule 1 covers TCP port 443 only. Rule 2 covers TCP port 3389. A rule does match, so the default drop does not apply.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Rule 5 matches and the query is allowed

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the firewall rules. The administrator's PC, 10.20.30.10, tries to open a Remote Desktop (RDP, TCP 3389) session to the server 10.20.0.70, but the connection is blocked even though rule 3 allows it. What is the fix?

options.text: Change rule 3's action from Allow to Deny
Move rule 3 above rule 2, because rule 2 matches first and denies the connection
Change the RDP port in rule 3 to 443

solution.explanation: The firewall applies the first matching rule. The RDP packet matches rule 2 (any source, any destination, TCP 3389), which denies it, so rule 3 is never checked. Placing the specific allow rule (rule 3) before the general deny (rule 2) lets only the administrator's RDP through.
steps: Specific allow must come before general deny
solution.why_others_wrong: Making rule 3 a Deny blocks the administrator permanently. Rule 5 is for DNS and is irrelevant. RDP listens on 3389, not 443.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Move rule 3 above rule 2, because rule 2 matches first and denies the connection

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft Learn: Remote Desktop uses RDP and listens on port 3389 by default.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the firewall rules. A guest laptop on the separate guest network 10.20.31.5 tries to open the HTTPS site 203.0.113.80 on TCP port 443. What happens?

options.text: It is dropped, because no rule matches and the firewall's default is to deny
It is allowed by rule 1, because the port is 443
It is allowed, because HTTPS is always permitted

solution.explanation: Rule 1 allows port 443 only from 10.20.30.0/24 (10.20.30.0 to 10.20.30.255); 10.20.31.5 is outside it. No other rule matches TCP 443, so the connection reaches the end of the list and is dropped by the default (implicit) deny.
solution.why_others_wrong: Rule 1 requires the source to be in the branch LAN. Rule 2 is about port 3389. No firewall permits a port automatically; only the rules decide.
solution.final_answer: Option A: It is dropped, because no rule matches and the firewall's default is to deny

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the firewall rules. A clerk's PC opens a connection to a website on port 443 (allowed by rule 1). There is no rule allowing traffic FROM the website back to the PC, yet the web pages arrive. Why?

options.text: Replies to port 443 are never checked by any firewall
The router converts the replies into DNS traffic
The stateful firewall records the allowed outgoing connection and automatically lets its reply packets back in

solution.explanation: A stateful firewall keeps a table of active connections. Packets that belong to a connection it has already allowed (the replies) are passed without needing their own rule, while unsolicited incoming packets are still dropped.
steps: Outgoing connection allowed -> entry in state table
solution.why_others_wrong: A stateless packet filter would need an explicit return rule; it is the state table, not the port, that lets replies in. Rule 5 covers only DNS queries to 10.20.0.53. Routers do not turn web traffic into DNS.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The stateful firewall records the allowed outgoing connection and automatically lets its reply packets back in

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the firewall rules. Rule 4 allows branch PCs to reach the head-office mail server 10.20.0.25 on TCP port 993. What do the PCs' email programs use this port for?

options.text: Sending mail with SMTP message submission
Downloading mail with POP3 over TLS
Reading mailboxes with IMAP over TLS (IMAPS)
Opening the bank's website over HTTPS

solution.explanation: Port 993 is the default port of IMAP over implicit TLS ('imaps'), used to read and manage mailboxes on the server over an encrypted connection.
solution.why_others_wrong: Message submission uses 587 (or 465 with implicit TLS). POP3 over TLS uses 995. HTTPS uses 443.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Reading mailboxes with IMAP over TLS (IMAPS)

fact_checks.claim: RFC 8314: imaps default port 993; pop3s default port 995; submissions default port 465.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which is the largest example of a WAN (Wide Area Network), linking networks across countries and continents?

solution.explanation: A WAN covers a large geographical area. The Internet, a worldwide network of networks, is the largest WAN.
steps: Worldwide network of networks = Internet = largest WAN
solution.why_others_wrong: A LAN covers a building or branch, a PAN a few metres around a person, and home Wi-Fi a single house.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A cable-broadband connection reaches a branch through a round cable with a central copper conductor, an insulating layer, a braided metal shield and an outer jacket. Which cable is this?

solution.explanation: Coaxial cable has one central conductor surrounded by insulation and a metal shield on the same axis. It is used for cable TV and cable broadband.
steps: Central conductor + shield on the same axis = coaxial
solution.why_others_wrong: Twisted pair has pairs of wires twisted together. Fibre carries light in glass strands. Ribbon cable is flat, used inside computers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A new branch PC joins the network and gets its IP address automatically from a DHCP server. In what order are the four DHCP messages exchanged?

solution.explanation: The client broadcasts DHCPDISCOVER; servers reply with DHCPOFFER; the client broadcasts DHCPREQUEST for the chosen offer; the chosen server confirms with DHCPACK.
solution.why_others_wrong: The client must discover servers before any offer, and it requests only after receiving an offer.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge

fact_checks.claim: RFC 2131 section 3.1: the client broadcasts DHCPDISCOVER, servers respond with DHCPOFFER, the client broadcasts DHCPREQUEST, and the server responds with DHCPACK.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A small bank network uses RIP, a distance-vector routing protocol that counts hops. A network that is 16 hops away is treated as unreachable. What is the largest network diameter RIP supports?

solution.explanation: RIP uses hop count as its metric and treats a metric of 16 as infinity (unreachable), so it is limited to networks whose longest path is 15 hops. The small limit helps end counting-to-infinity loops quickly.
solution.why_others_wrong: 16 is the 'unreachable' value, not a usable distance. 255 is the maximum IPv4 TTL, not RIP's limit. RIP is deliberately limited.

fact_checks.claim: RFC 2453: the protocol is limited to networks whose longest path is 15 hops; the value 16 (infinity) indicates the destination is not reachable.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Every IPv6-enabled branch PC automatically has an address beginning with fe80:: on each interface, usable only to talk to devices on the same link (for example, the local router). What type of address is it?

options.text: Global unicast address, routable on the internet
Link-local unicast address (fe80::/10), which routers never forward to other links
Loopback address of the PC itself

solution.explanation: fe80::/10 is the IPv6 link-local prefix. Every interface configures such an address automatically; it is used for neighbour discovery and routing protocols on the local link, and routers must not forward packets with link-local source or destination to other links.
steps: Valid only on the local link
solution.why_others_wrong: Global unicast addresses (typically from 2000::/3) are internet-routable. IPv6 multicast addresses begin with ff. The loopback address is ::1.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Link-local unicast address (fe80::/10), which routers never forward to other links

fact_checks.claim: RFC 4291: Link-Local unicast prefix is FE80::/10; routers must not forward any packets with link-local source or destination addresses to other links.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In the email address loans.pune@bank.example, which symbol separates the mailbox (user) name from the domain name?

solution.explanation: An email address has the form local-part@domain: 'loans.pune' is the mailbox and 'bank.example' is the domain whose mail server receives the message.
solution.why_others_wrong: #, / and & are not used to separate the parts of an email address.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A circular's link is https://bank.example/rules.html#section4. When the browser requests the page, which part of the address is NOT sent to the web server?

options.text: #section4 (the fragment), which the browser uses to jump to that part of the page

solution.explanation: The fragment starts with # and identifies a part of the resource. The browser requests /rules.html from bank.example over HTTPS, then scrolls to the element 'section4' itself; the fragment never goes to the server.
steps: Fragment (#...) handled only by the browser
solution.why_others_wrong: The scheme decides the protocol used, the host is where the request goes, and the path is the resource requested; all are used to make the request.
solution.final_answer: Option B: #section4 (the fragment), which the browser uses to jump to that part of the page

fact_checks.claim: MDN: the fragment is the last part of the URI, starting with #; it is not sent to the server when the URI is requested and is processed by the client.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A fintech app calls a bank's balance API 500 times in one minute. The API starts answering with HTTP status 429. What does this mean, and what should the app do?

options.text: Unauthorized: the API key is wrong
Not Found: the API address has changed
Internal Server Error: the bank's server has crashed
Too Many Requests: the client is being rate-limited and should slow down and retry later

solution.explanation: 429 Too Many Requests (RFC 6585) says the user has sent too many requests in a given time (rate limiting). The server may send a Retry-After header; the client should back off and retry later.
solution.why_others_wrong: Wrong credentials give 401, a missing resource 404, and a server fault 500. None of these is about the request rate.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Too Many Requests: the client is being rate-limited and should slow down and retry later

fact_checks.claim: RFC 6585 section 4: the 429 status code indicates that the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time ('rate limiting').

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A net-banking site sends the response header  Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'  with every page. What protection does this give?

options.text: It forces the browser to use HTTPS for all future visits
It encrypts the cookies stored in the browser
The browser runs only scripts loaded from the site's own origin, which blocks most injected (XSS) scripts
It stops other websites from showing the bank's pages in a frame

solution.explanation: CSP tells the browser which sources of content are allowed. script-src 'self' permits JavaScript only from the page's own origin, so inline or third-party scripts injected by an attacker are not executed. Its main use is to reduce cross-site scripting (XSS).
solution.why_others_wrong: Forcing HTTPS is HSTS. Cookies are not encrypted by CSP. Framing control is done by the frame-ancestors directive or X-Frame-Options, not by script-src.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The browser runs only scripts loaded from the site's own origin, which blocks most injected (XSS) scripts

fact_checks.claim: MDN: CSP controls which resources, especially JavaScript, a document may load; it is mainly a defence against XSS and is delivered in the Content-Security-Policy response header.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the cyber-cell complaints. In complaint 1, how did the fraudster get control of Mr. P's banking session, and what is the right advice?

options.text: The 'support app' was a remote-access (screen-sharing) app; never install such apps or share their codes at a caller's request
The phone's SIM was swapped; change the SIM card
The bank's server was hacked; nothing could have prevented it
A virus came through the phone's charger

solution.explanation: Screen-sharing or remote-access apps let another person see, and sometimes control, the phone. By getting the access code, the fraudster watched the screen (including OTPs and PINs) while the customer used the banking app. Banks never ask customers to install such apps.
steps: Caller asks to install app + share code
solution.why_others_wrong: The SIM was not changed; Mr. P kept his signal. The bank's systems were used normally with Mr. P's own credentials. Nothing points to a charging-port attack.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The 'support app' was a remote-access (screen-sharing) app; never install such apps or share their codes at a caller's request

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the cyber-cell complaints. Which attack does complaint 2 describe, and which control would most likely have stopped the loss?

options.text: Business email compromise (BEC); confirming any change of a supplier's bank details by calling the supplier on a number already on record

solution.explanation: BEC impersonates a trusted business contact (here, through a look-alike domain) to divert payments, often by announcing 'new bank details'. Independent verification through a known phone number before changing payee details defeats it.
steps: Look-alike supplier domain + 'new bank account' = BEC
solution.why_others_wrong: No files were encrypted (ransomware), no DNS was tampered with (pharming), and no computing power was stolen (cryptojacking).
solution.final_answer: Option B: Business email compromise (BEC); confirming any change of a supplier's bank details by calling the supplier on a number already on record

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the cyber-cell complaints. What made the call in complaint 3 convincing?

options.text: A keylogger on the manager's PC
A logic bomb in the payment system
An AI-generated deepfake (cloned) voice of the regional head, built from his recordings

solution.explanation: Deepfake audio uses machine learning trained on samples of a person's voice to produce new speech in that voice. Combined with urgency and authority, it is a powerful form of vishing; a call-back on a known number or a code word defeats it.
steps: Synthetic voice imitating a real person = deepfake voice cloning
solution.why_others_wrong: A keylogger records keystrokes. A forged certificate concerns websites. A logic bomb is hidden code triggered by a condition. None imitates a voice.
solution.final_answer: Option D: An AI-generated deepfake (cloned) voice of the regional head, built from his recordings

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the cyber-cell complaints. Complaint 4 describes card data being stolen from a genuine HTTPS checkout page by an injected script. What is this attack called, and why did HTTPS not prevent it?

options.text: Formjacking (digital / web skimming); the malicious script runs inside the genuine page in the customer's browser, so it reads the data before it is encrypted for sending
Card skimming at an ATM; HTTPS does not cover ATMs
Man-in-the-middle attack; HTTPS was switched off
SQL injection; HTTPS does not protect databases

solution.explanation: In formjacking, attackers add JavaScript to a legitimate site's payment form (often through a compromised third-party script). The script runs in the shopper's browser with the page's own privileges and copies the card details as they are typed, then sends them out. HTTPS protects data in transit, not data that a script on the page itself reads. Content Security Policy, script integrity checks and monitoring of page changes are defences.
steps: Reads form fields in the browser
solution.why_others_wrong: ATM skimming uses a physical device on the card slot. A man-in-the-middle attack intercepts traffic, but here the connection was genuine HTTPS. SQL injection attacks the database through input, not a script in the page.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Formjacking (digital / web skimming); the malicious script runs inside the genuine page in the customer's browser, so it reads the data before it is encrypted for sending

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An antivirus program finds a suspicious file and, instead of deleting it, moves it to a protected isolated area where it cannot run but can be restored if it turns out to be safe. What is this action called?

solution.explanation: Quarantine isolates a suspected file in a secure location so it cannot execute or spread, while keeping it in case it is a false alarm.
solution.why_others_wrong: Formatting erases a whole drive. Defragmentation rearranges file pieces. Compression reduces size.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank hires security professionals, with written permission, to try to break into its systems and report the weaknesses so that they can be fixed. These authorised testers are known as:

solution.explanation: White-hat or ethical hackers test systems with the owner's permission (for example in penetration tests) to find and fix weaknesses before criminals exploit them.
steps: Authorised, to improve security = white hat
solution.why_others_wrong: Black-hat hackers break in illegally for gain. Script kiddies use others' tools without skill. Hacktivists attack for political or social causes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A customer's phone shows the bank's genuine helpline number on an incoming call, but the caller is a fraudster. The fraudster has falsified the number displayed to the receiver. What is this technique called?

solution.explanation: Caller ID spoofing makes a call appear to come from a trusted number. Customers should not trust the displayed number alone and should call back on the official number themselves.
steps: Fake number displayed = caller ID spoofing
solution.why_others_wrong: Shoulder surfing is watching someone type. Tailgating is following someone through a secure door. Juice jacking is an attack through public USB charging ports.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A loan officer must use long, different passwords for twelve bank systems. Which tool safely stores them in an encrypted vault, unlocked by one master password, and can generate strong new ones?

solution.explanation: A password manager keeps credentials in an encrypted vault, fills them in on the right sites, and generates strong unique passwords, so users do not reuse or write down passwords.
solution.why_others_wrong: A plain spreadsheet or sticky notes expose the passwords to anyone who sees them. Browser history records visited pages, not passwords.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A customer approves a large RTGS transfer with a digital signature made with her private key. Later she claims she never sent the instruction. The signature lets the bank prove that only her key could have signed it. Which security property is this?

solution.explanation: Non-repudiation means the sender cannot credibly deny having sent a message. Because a digital signature can be created only with the signer's private key, a valid signature is evidence that she authorised the instruction.
solution.why_others_wrong: Availability is about systems being usable when needed. Anonymity is the opposite of proving identity. Compression reduces size and has nothing to do with proof.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: An insider hides confidential customer data inside the pixels of an ordinary-looking holiday photo and emails it out. The picture looks normal, and nobody suspects that it carries hidden data. What is this technique?

solution.explanation: Steganography hides the existence of a message by embedding it in another file (image, audio, video), for example in the least significant bits of pixels. Encryption hides the content; steganography hides the fact that there is a message at all.
steps: Data hidden inside a normal-looking image = steganography
solution.why_others_wrong: Hashing makes a fixed-length digest. Tokenisation replaces card numbers with tokens. Phishing is a deceptive message aimed at victims.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's security team sets up a fake server that looks like a poorly protected payments database but holds no real data. Any connection to it is suspicious, and the team studies the attackers' methods. What is this decoy called?

solution.explanation: A honeypot is a deliberately exposed decoy system used to attract attackers, detect intrusions and learn their tools and techniques, without risking real data.
steps: Decoy system to lure and study attackers = honeypot
solution.why_others_wrong: A firewall filters traffic. A proxy forwards requests for clients. A load balancer spreads traffic over real servers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the Staff table. Which names does this query return?

SELECT e.name FROM Staff e JOIN Staff m ON e.manager_id = m.emp_id WHERE e.salary > m.salary;

solution.explanation: The table is joined to itself: e is the employee and m is that employee's manager. Comparing each salary with the manager's: Ravi 60,000 < Asha 90,000; Meena 75,000 < 90,000; John 75,000 = Meena 75,000 (not greater); Farah 62,000 > Ravi 60,000; Kiran < Meena; Neha < Asha; Tara < Neha. Asha has no manager, so she has no join row. Only Farah qualifies.
solution.why_others_wrong: John's salary equals his manager's, so the strict > excludes him. 'No rows' ignores Farah.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the Staff table. How many rows does this query count?

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Staff WHERE COALESCE(manager_id, 'E1') = 'E1';

solution.explanation: COALESCE returns its first non-NULL argument, so Asha's NULL manager_id becomes 'E1' for this test. Rows with 'E1': Asha (from NULL), Ravi, Meena and Neha = 4.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 is what manager_id = 'E1' alone gives, because NULL = 'E1' is not true. 1 counts only the NULL row. 5 adds a row that does not match.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

solution.explanation: Without a join condition, every row of Staff is paired with every row of Branches: 8 x 3 = 24 rows.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11 adds the row counts. 8 and 3 are the sizes of the individual tables.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the Staff table. Which names does this correlated subquery return?

SELECT name FROM Staff s WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM Staff WHERE branch = s.branch);

solution.explanation: The inner query is re-evaluated for each outer row, using that row's branch. Pune average = (90,000 + 60,000 + 62,000) / 3 = 70,666.67 -> Asha. Delhi average = (75,000 + 75,000 + 48,000) / 3 = 66,000 -> Meena and John. Agra average = (52,000 + 40,000) / 2 = 46,000 -> Neha.
solution.why_others_wrong: Asha, Meena and John is the result of comparing with the overall average (62,750), which ignores the branch condition. The other options miss someone in Pune or Agra.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Asha, Meena, John and Neha

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the Staff table. What value does this query show for Farah?

SELECT name, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk FROM Staff;

solution.explanation: Order: Asha 90,000 (1); Meena and John 75,000 tie (both 2); Farah 62,000. DENSE_RANK leaves no gap after a tie, so Farah gets 3. (RANK would skip to 4.)
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 is what RANK gives, skipping a number after the tie. 2 is the tied rank above her. 5 counts her row position wrongly.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In an old file system, a customer's address is stored separately in the savings, loan and locker files, so the same data appears three times and may not match after one copy is changed. What is the repeated storage of the same data called?

solution.explanation: Data redundancy is the unnecessary duplication of the same data in several places. It wastes space and leads to inconsistency when only some copies are updated; a DBMS reduces it by storing each fact once.
solution.why_others_wrong: Data independence means programs are unaffected by changes in how data is stored. Encryption protects data. Compression reduces its size.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the ATM register. An Indian IFSC has 11 characters, and its first four letters identify the bank. What does =LEFT(A2, 4) return?

solution.explanation: LEFT(text, n) returns the first n characters. The first 4 characters of PMBK0004521 are PMBK, the bank code. (The fifth character of an IFSC is 0 and the last six identify the branch.)
solution.why_others_wrong: PMBK0 has five characters. 4521 and 0004521 are taken from the right side (as RIGHT would do).

fact_checks.claim: RBI NEFT FAQ: IFSC is an 11-character code; the first four alphabetic characters represent the bank, the fifth character is 0 and the last six characters represent the branch.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the ATM register. Each cash cassette holds at most Rs 10,00,000. To find how many cassettes ATM-PN-01 needs for its load, the clerk enters =ROUNDUP(D2/1000000, 0). What does it return?

solution.explanation: D2 / 1,000,000 = 2,350,000 / 1,000,000 = 2.35. ROUNDUP rounds away from zero to 0 decimal places, giving 3 (two cassettes cannot hold Rs 23.5 lakh).
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 is what ROUND or INT would give, leaving Rs 3.5 lakh without a cassette. 2.35 ignores the rounding. 4 over-rounds.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: ROUNDUP rounds a number up, away from 0 (zero).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the ATM register. Given that 26-Oct-2026 (cell C2) is a Monday, what does =TEXT(C4, "dddd") return?

solution.concept: TEXT function with date format codes
solution.explanation: The format code dddd shows the full name of the weekday. C4 is 31-Oct-2026, five days after Monday 26-Oct, so it is a Saturday.
solution.why_others_wrong: Friday and Sunday are a day off. '31' would be the result of the code d or dd (day of the month).

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft TEXT function: =TEXT(TODAY(),"DDDD") returns today's day of the week, like Monday.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Refer to the ATM register. What does =NETWORKDAYS(C2, C7, G2) return? (NETWORKDAYS counts working days from the start date to the end date, both included, leaving out Saturdays, Sundays and the listed holidays.)

solution.explanation: From Monday 26-Oct to Thursday 05-Nov 2026: 26-30 Oct gives 5 weekdays, 2-5 Nov gives 4 weekdays, total 9. The holiday in G2 (Monday 02-Nov) is removed: 9 - 1 = 8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 9 forgets the holiday. 7 also leaves out the start date. 11 counts every calendar day.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: NETWORKDAYS returns the number of whole working days between start_date and end_date; working days exclude weekends and dates identified in holidays (example: 1-Oct-2012 to 1-Mar-2013 = 110, used to confirm both ends are counted).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text:
Refer to the ATM register. A clerk writes this formula for row 5:

=IFS(E5/D5>=0.6, "Watch", E5/D5>=0.9, "Reload today", TRUE, "OK")

What does it return?

solution.concept: IFS returns the first TRUE condition
solution.explanation: E5 / D5 = 1,710,000 / 1,800,000 = 0.95. IFS checks the conditions in order and returns the value of the FIRST one that is TRUE. 0.95 >= 0.6 is already TRUE, so the result is 'Watch', even though 0.95 >= 0.9 is also true. The tests should be written from the strictest (>= 0.9) down.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Reload today' would need the 0.9 test to come first. 'OK' is reached only when both tests fail. #N/A appears only when no condition is TRUE, but here TRUE is the last test anyway.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: IFS returns a value that corresponds to the first TRUE condition; if no TRUE conditions are found, it returns #N/A.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: During a PowerPoint slide show, a trainer wants the screen to go completely black for a while to hold the audience's attention, and then to return to the same slide. Which key does this (on Windows)?

solution.explanation: Pressing B (or the full stop key) shows a blank black screen; pressing it again returns to the presentation at the same slide.
solution.why_others_wrong: W shows a blank WHITE screen. Esc ends the slide show. Home jumps to the first slide.

solution.why_others_wrong: Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus. The other combinations do not change case.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In Excel for Windows, a clerk selects a block of loan data and wants to convert it into an Excel Table with banded rows, filter buttons and automatic expansion for new rows. Which shortcut opens the Create Table dialog?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: In a long loan agreement, a paragraph sometimes leaves just its first line alone at the bottom of a page, or just its last line alone at the top of the next page. Which paragraph setting in Word (Paragraph > Line and Page Breaks) prevents these single stranded lines?

solution.explanation: Widow/Orphan control stops Word from printing the last line of a paragraph by itself at the top of a page (a widow) or the first line by itself at the bottom of a page (an orphan); it moves an extra line so at least two stay together. It is on by default.
steps: Single line stranded at page top/bottom = widow/orphan
solution.why_others_wrong: Keep with next keeps a paragraph on the same page as the next one (used for headings). Page break before always starts the paragraph on a new page. Suppress line numbers hides line numbering.

fact_checks.claim: Microsoft: Widow/Orphan control is a Pagination option on the Line and Page Breaks tab of the Paragraph dialog and is turned on by default.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: Which NPCI-operated system lets customers pay electricity, water, gas and telecom bills of many billers through banks, apps and agent outlets in one interoperable network, with instant confirmation?

solution.explanation: BBPS, conceived by the RBI and run by NPCI, is an interoperable bill-payment system: a customer can pay many billers' bills through any participating bank, app or agent and get instant confirmation.
solution.why_others_wrong: RTGS is RBI's large-value funds transfer system. AePS is Aadhaar-based cash withdrawal and transfer. NACH handles bulk debits and credits such as salaries and EMIs.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS)

fact_checks.claim: NPCI: Bharat Bill Payment System, an RBI-conceptualised interoperable bill-payment system operated by NPCI, covering electricity, water, gas and telecom bills with instant confirmation (pilot launched 2016).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A shopper wants to pay a merchant by scanning a UPI QR code but have the amount charged to her credit card rather than her savings account. Which type of credit card can be linked to a UPI ID for this purpose?

options.text: Only a corporate card of an international network
No credit card; UPI works only with bank accounts

solution.explanation: NPCI allows RuPay credit cards to be linked to UPI IDs in UPI apps. The customer sets a UPI PIN for the card and can then pay merchants by scanning QR codes, with the amount billed to the card.
steps: Credit card linked on UPI = RuPay credit card
solution.why_others_wrong: Foreign-issued cards cannot be linked to UPI. The facility is for RuPay credit cards. UPI is no longer limited to bank accounts.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A RuPay credit card

fact_checks.claim: NPCI 'RuPay Credit Card on UPI': customers can link RuPay credit cards to a UPI ID on UPI apps; only RuPay credit cards are eligible.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question_text: A bank's PIN pads encrypt each customer's PIN with a different key for every transaction, all derived from one base key held securely at the bank, so that if one transaction key is ever exposed, past and future transactions remain protected. Which key-management scheme is this?

options.text: A single static key shared by every terminal

solution.explanation: DUKPT gives each transaction a unique key derived from a base derivation key; the terminal sends a key serial number so the host can re-derive the key. Compromise of one derived key does not reveal keys of past or future transactions.
steps: Unique key per transaction from a base key = DUKPT
solution.why_others_wrong: A shared static key exposes every terminal if leaked. ROT13 is a trivial letter substitution, not encryption. MD5 is a broken hash and is not reversible encryption of the PIN.
solution.final_answer: Option D: DUKPT (Derived Unique Key Per Transaction)

fact_checks.claim: DUKPT: for every transaction a unique key is used which is derived from a fixed key; if a derived key is compromised, future and past transaction data are still protected.
